_comment: The scoring vocabulary of the Indonesian regulation corpus · VOCABULARY_PATH.
! This file is the corpus's, not the engine's. Vera is a retrieval engine,
not a legal one: `authority` asks how binding a source is, `structural`
asks whether a chunk is operative text or an appendix, and neither question
is Indonesian. Only the answers below are.
! It duplicates `identity.authority` in Ravel's
registry/profiles/id_regulation@1.0.yaml, which is the copy that should
win. The destination for this data is `corpus_meta`, written by Ravel from
that profile at ingest, beside the model and pooling the corpus already
declares. Until that schema change lands this file is how the capability is
reachable -- and while two copies exist they can drift, which is exactly the
argument for finishing the move.
! Loading this file reproduces the compiled-in fallback exactly. It is here
as the worked example and as the migration's first step, not because the
current deployment needs it.
Authority follows UU 12/2011: the Art 7 ladder (UU > PP > Perpres > Perda
Provinsi > Perda Kab/Kota), with Art 8 instruments -- a governor's,
regent's or mayor's own regulation -- BELOW the Perda they implement.
! Fitted against both this table and one that inverts that last pair,
Recall@5 is identical (57.5% in-sample, 47.5% leave-one-out at n=40). The
fine ordering is NOT evidence-backed here. It is correct anyway, because a
table stating something legally false is wrong whether or not a 40-case
eval set can detect it (docs/EVAL.md §5).
max_tier is 10 and no entry reaches it: the scale is the published
hierarchy (UUD 1945 = 9), not the set of types this corpus happens to hold.
Normalising against what is loaded would make the same chunk score
differently in a corpus that merely lacks a constitution.

structural._note: 80,121 of 355,621 indexable chunks are LAMPIRAN -- 22.5% of the corpus is annex material: tables, forms and schedules that are rarely the answer to a question about obligations.
structural.label: LAMPIRAN

structural._note: Elucidation explains a clause authoritatively without being one, so it sits between an annex and an article.
structural.label: PENJELASAN

structural._note: A prefix rule, not a substring one. 'Pasal 9 dihapus' is an amending clause that contains the word without being one -- the same distinction Ravel's profile makes with marker_only.
structural.label: PASAL

_note: ! `dapat`, `harus`, `wajib` and `tidak` are here because they occur in nearly every chunk and carry no discriminative power AS TERMS. That is correct for term overlap, and is precisely why a separate modality factor is worth building: 'query asks for an obligation AND chunk states an obligation' is discriminative even though neither word is.
